prerequisites: Knowledge and skills developed in Technical Drawing II from Baccalaureate, or Technical Drawing I and II from the corresponding Professional Module.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the importance of graphic representation in the exercise of the engineering profession for the transmission of technological knowledge.
Develop spatial mental faculties and the sense of ordering external objects, thus strengthening the student's creative capacity through a graphic language.
Be able to apply graphic representation techniques using computer-aided design programs.
Be able to graphically solve problems that arise in the execution of industrial and infrastructure projects and express them in the document (plans).

syllabus_topics: MODULE 1.- REPRESENTATION TECHNIQUES: DIHEDRAL AND QUOTED SYSTEMS - Topic 1. THE UNIVERSAL LANGUAGE IN GRAPHIC ENGINEERING. EXECUTION METHODS: The role of technical drawing in the design process. Fundamental concepts. Design tools. Visualization and information presentation techniques.
Topic 2. METRIC GEOMETRY: Loci. Geometric constructions. Scales. Transformations. Applications.
Topic 3. DIHEDRAL SYSTEM: Fundamentals and applications. Representation, belonging, particular positions. European and American systems. Applications.
Topic 4. DIHEDRAL SYSTEM: Intersections, Parallelism and perpendicularity. Applications to Technical Drawing.
Topic 5. DIHEDRAL SYSTEM: True magnitudes. Applications to Industrial Technical Drawing.
Topic 6. TECHNICAL CURVES: Planar curves (conical and cyclic). Three-dimensional curves (Bsplines, Splines, cyclic). Applications.
Topic 7. SURFACES: Ruled surfaces. Freeform surfaces (Bézier, Nurbs). Applications.
Topic 8. QUOTED SYSTEM: Fundamentals and applications.
Topic 9. TOPOGRAPHIC DRAWING: Cartographic and topographic plans. Applications to construction technical drawing (Roofs, Earthworks, Roads).
Topic 10. INTERSECTION OF SURFACES: General considerations. Constructive geometry of bodies. Spatial situation. Applications in manufacturing and building.

MODULE 2.- TECHNICAL DRAWING - Topic 11. STANDARDIZED EXECUTION METHODS: Types of technical drawings. Formats. Representation of industrial forms (European and American Systems). Views (particular, partial and auxiliary). Sketching. Applications.
Topic 12. STANDARDIZED VIEWS: Fundamental rules. Cuts. Sections. Applications.
Topic 13. TRUE MAGNITUDES: Revolved sections. Auxiliary views. Simplified views. Applications.
Topic 14. DIMENSIONING: General principles. Dimensioning rules. Criteria for dimension selection. Applications.
Topic 15. ASSEMBLY DRAWING: Bill of materials. Standardized components. Plan interpretation.

MODULE 3.- COMPUTER-AIDED DESIGN - Topic 16. CONCEPTS OF COMPUTER-AIDED DESIGN: Introduction (vector and bitmap systems). Software. Peripherals. Applications to Technical Drawing. Working environment. Initial settings. Layer and line type organization. Document management.
Topic 17. 2D REPRESENTATION: Drawing entities. Editing tools. Texts. Applications.
Topic 18. DIMENSIONING: Symbolism. Settings. Styles. Types. Applications.
Topic 19. 3D OBJECT REPRESENTATION: Types of modeling (Surfaces and Solids). Meshes. Editing tools. Visualization (textures, lighting).
Topic 20. PRODUCT INFORMATION ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER: Graphic information exchange standards. Image import. Plan generation. Document printing.
PRACTICES - TECHNICAL DRAWING PRACTICES (Module 2): Execution of standardized views with cuts and sections in standardized formats.
PRACTICES - TECHNICAL DRAWING PRACTICES (Module 2): Standardized dimensioning of "part plans".
PRACTICES - TECHNICAL DRAWING PRACTICES (Module 2): Standardized execution of "simple mechanical assembly" plans.
PRACTICES - CAD PRACTICES (Module 3): Design of 2D Plans. Drawing and dimensioning. Generation of standardized presentations.
PRACTICES - CAD PRACTICES (Module 3): 3D modeling of parts. Generation of Plans with standardized views, cuts and sections.
assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must achieve at least 25% in the written tests and 50% in the sum of all assessment systems. If this critical evaluation criterion is not met, the total course grade will be FAIL, with the resulting score from the sum of all assessment systems truncated to a maximum of 4.5 points. For students with recognized part-time study dedication, non-recoverable activities may be replaced by similar activities with different deadlines or equivalent evaluation tests, provided the reason is the same as for their part-time status.
